newsitem.title: UK: Car shuttle resumes in Channel tunnel after fire.
newsitem.headline: Car shuttle resumes in Channel tunnel after fire.

text.p: Passenger car service resumed through the tunnel under the English Channel Tuesday, three weeks after a fire closed down the undersea link between Britain and France.

The first Le Shuttle train, carrying 61 vehicles, left the Coquelles terminal near Calais at 6:30 a.m. and arrived at the Cheriton terminal in England 50 minutes later. The crossing took about 15 minutes longer than before the accident due to fire damage in the tunnel.
The tunnel was closed to all traffic Nov. 18, when a fire on a truck destroyed a freight train and severely damaged a section of the tunnel, injuring 34 people.
Limited rail service for passengers between Paris and London and Brussels and London resumed last Wednesday using one of the two parallel rail tunnels. The other one is still closed for repairs.
In Paris, tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA said customer bookings for its Le Shuttle passenger service were exceeding its expectations.
"We have had a customer response beyond our hopes," a Eurotunnel spokeswoman said. "We have a problem of allocating places."
Eurotunnel is running three departures every two hours under the current reduced service, using cross-over points in the twin-bore tunnel to bypass a section badly damaged by the fire.
